findings.failure_path: A completion is accepted and its tool call passes current-policy re-authorization under generation g; before the handler begins the irreversible external action, a concurrent revocation advances the generation to g+1. The rule makes generation advancement atomic and requires re-authorization sometime before the side effect, but it does not atomically couple the final generation comparison to side-effect admission or fence already accepted/queued calls. The call can therefore execute after its authority was revoked.
findings.smallest_fix: Require side-effect admission and the final current-generation comparison to share the same atomic serialization boundary as revocation. Advancing the generation must fence or cancel accepted-but-not-started calls; only a call admitted under an unchanged generation may enter the irreversible handler.

challenge_focus: Adversarial pass on the lane-5 candidate: (1) atomic generation advance and re-authorization — an ordering where an in-flight completion is accepted before the generation advances, or a re-authorization that checks the tool but not destination, arguments, or data scope; (2) eviction-vs-invalidation, normalized cache counters, batch capability decision, tool-set boundary, plan-then-execute binding — any surviving path to a revoked call, a double count, duplicate billing, in-flight mutation, or an injected external action; (3) the fan-out gate's shared-write versus read-only distinction, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission or over-broad cost; (4) register anchors, receipts, rows — stale locators, unsupported claims, contradictions, a row citing two owners; (5) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
